t1_read_text.detail: Dock semantics are RICH and exact: mixer channels with live values ('Desktop Audio' -3.2 dB, 'Mic/Aux' -15.0 dB '(actuellement muet)', 'nvidia broadcast' -9.8 dB), scene list ('comming soon' [selected=True] …), sources, transition, controls — every value cross-checked against the pixels.

t2_enumerate.detail: 185 nodes: buttons, sliders (with values), checkboxes (mute state), lists with selection. Qt maps QWidget semantics to UIA correctly wherever a widget IS the content.

t5_blind_action.detail: The safe-mode dialog: a coordinate click FAILED (contested pixel space — another window covered the point; the hit-test guard caught it), while InvokePattern succeeded with no coordinates at all. Semantic actions bypass pixel-space contention — and are precisely what the action-allowlist must gate (cf. the macOS AXPress stopwatch incident).

t6_pictorial.detail: THE SILENT CELL THIS CAMPAIGN WAS HUNTING. The video preview renders 'On arrive bientôt' (a text source composited by OBS's GL pipeline) — plainly visible on screen. The UIA tree covers that area with an UNNAMED QWidget group: no text, no [pixels]/image marker, no 'I cannot read this' signal. A consumer asking 'what does the preview show?' reads 'nothing there' and is WRONG, with no in-channel warning. Contrast the explicit declarations elsewhere: browser '[pixels] canvas', Paint's named canvas group, Chromium-UIA's '[pixels] image'. Qt is not lying about widget content — it is silent about non-widget content.

measurements.notes: Cost break-even (1229 vs 1275 tok), capture 470-640 ms — the slowest bridge measured (Qt proxies every property call). THE FINDING: the first genuinely silent-class divergence of the Windows campaign, in Qt's accessibility bridge on a real app — the video-preview region is an anonymous container while the screen shows readable text inside it. Honest qualifications: (1) predictable a priori — the Qt signature + app category (video compositor) tells a router in advance that pictorial regions will be UNMARKED, and OBS's preview rect is discoverable as 'large unnamed leaf container'; (2) mitigable at runtime — PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) captures the window's own surface without focus for a spot-check (technique added to the probe library during this cell); (3) the divergence is one of omission-without-declaration, not fabrication. Under the campaign's own standard (a view that disagrees with the screen without declaring it) it is recorded as silent, not excused. Op incidents kept: our force-kill triggered OBS's safe-mode dialog; foreground acquisition failed while the elevated Task Manager held focus — PrintWindow made ground truth possible anyway.
